description:
Overview

The Maastricht University (UM) NL-High Potential Scholarship programme offers 18 full scholarships each academic year to highly talented students from outside the EU/EEA who have been admitted to a participating full-time, English-taught master’s programme at UM. It combines the High Potential Scholarship (funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund) with the NL Scholarship (funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science).

This is one of the strongest fully funded master’s options in the Netherlands: it covers tuition, living expenses, insurance and visa costs. Competition is very high — the university notes that only about 2% of applicants receive an award.

What the Scholarship Covers

UM NL-High Potential Scholarship components (2027-2028)
ItemDetails
Living expenses€20,150 for a 13-month one-year master’s (about €1,550/month), or €38,750 for a 25-month two-year master’s. Paid to students by the UM International Services Desk.
Health & liability insurance€700 — arranged and paid by UM International Services Desk.
Visa application costsAt cost — arranged and paid by UM International Services Desk.
Tuition feesAt cost — arranged and paid by UM International Services Desk.
Pre-Academic Training costsAt cost — arranged and paid by UM International Services Desk.
International Student Ambassador ProgrammeAt cost for the first block.
AccommodationA room is allocated until 16 July 2028 and is a mandatory part of the scholarship; refusing the room cancels the award. Not suitable for partners, children or pets.

The €20,150 living-expense figure for a one-year programme is a total, roughly €1,550 per month, covering housing (€960), groceries and personal hygiene (€160), telephone (€60), travel (€100), books and study materials (€90), clothing/hobbies (€125) and miscellaneous (€55). Air tickets and an approximately €75 cleaning fee are not included.

Eligibility

  • You hold a nationality outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland or Suriname, and meet the requirements for a Dutch entry visa and residence permit. No dual EU/EEA or Swiss nationality.
  • You have applied for admission to a participating full-time master’s programme at UM for 2027-2028 and submitted a complete application file meeting all admission requirements by 10 December 2026.
  • You have never participated in a degree-seeking higher-education programme in the Netherlands (exchange programmes are welcome). Preference is given to candidates who do not yet hold a master’s degree.
  • You are not older than 35 on 1 September 2027.
  • You have excellent prior results: a GPA of 7.5 out of 10 or higher (about 75% or 3 out of 4, depending on your grading system).
  • You agree to become an active UM NL-High Potential and UM ambassador, including at least one information session for students or stakeholders.
  • You submit only one application for one scholarship; documents cannot be added or replaced after submission.

Application Timeline

Key dates and selection steps
ItemDetails
Applications open1 October 2026.
Master’s admission file deadline10 December 2026 (including any programme handling fee, which UM does not cover).
Scholarship deadline1 February 2027 at 23:59 CET. By this date all registration requirements except legal residence, tuition payment and a hard copy of your diploma must be met.
Completeness checkUM International Services Desk checks applications after 1 February 2027.
Faculty rankingFaculties rank their top five applicants in February 2027; final check in March 2027.

How to Apply

  • Apply through Studielink for an eligible participating master’s programme and receive your UM student ID — needed to submit the scholarship form.
  • Prepare an official document from your home university showing your most recent GPA and a document explaining your grading system.
  • Log in with your UM account and submit the official scholarship application form before 1 February 2027, 23:59 CET.

Official Link

Maastricht University — NL-High Potential Scholarship

Important Notes

  • Only 18 scholarships are available and selection is highly competitive (about 2% of applicants).
  • Confirm the award number, the 10 December admission deadline and your programme against the university’s own 2027-2028 participating-programmes list before paying any handling fee.
  • The allocated room is mandatory; the scholarship cannot be deferred and accommodation is not suitable for families or pets.
